Definition: properly, to spoil (literally, by breaking to pieces); figuratively, to make (or be) good for nothing, i.e. bad (physically, socially or morally)
BiblicalUsage: Lot pleads with the men of Sodom, do not so wickedly. Isaiah says wash you, make you clean, put away the evil of your doings, cease to do evil. Jeremiah says they did worse than their fathers, and the psalmist says fret not thyself to do evil. The word is to spoil, to make good for nothing — bad, physically, socially, morally.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe evil is not a force but a spoiling, and the word means to break a good thing to pieces. I hold that ceasing to do evil is the first command of the prophet, and God still says it to us: wash you, make you clean.
